feature_request: We need a better way to track who is the right person to contact in each country.

proposed_scope_in.item: Read-only 'Who to contact' card on the existing Country page. It shows one recommended contact for each of three contexts (general country engagement, each active Mission, each active Project), plus up to 2 ranked alternates per context.

Deterministic ranking computed at read time from existing data, with no manual designation. Order is: role match to the context, then affiliation to that Mission or Project, then most recent Engagement date, then alphabetical tiebreak. Each recommendation shows a one-line 'why' (e.g. 'Mission delegate, last engaged 12 days ago').

Staleness handling: contacts flagged inactive or past term end are excluded from ranking. Each shown contact displays 'last engaged N days ago' and gets a 'may be outdated' badge if there has been no Engagement in 180 days (a fixed constant, not a per-country setting).

The card reuses the existing Country/Mission access model: it shows only the contacts and fields the viewing user can already see on the Contact and Country records. No new permission rules are introduced.

Empty and fallback states: if no eligible contact exists for a context, show 'No current contact on record' with a link to the Country's existing contact list. Fall back from the Mission or Project context to the general country context, labelled as a fallback.

proposed_scope_out: Manual 'primary contact' designation or any extra fields Regional Coordinators must fill in
New tables or entities (reuses Country, Contact, Mission, Project, Engagement only)
ML or scoring models for contact recommendation
Approval, review, or verification workflows for recommendations
Cross-country dashboards, queues, or reports (e.g. 'countries with no contact')
Automated notifications, reminders, or outreach to confirm contact details
Protocol, seniority, or diplomatic-precedence ranking (a policy decision for humans, not product design)
Availability, time-zone, language, or preferred-channel handling
Escalation chains or formal backup-contact designation
Integrations with external directories or ministry data sources
Custom RBAC or new data-classification labels

assumptions.statement: 'Right person' depends on context, and three contexts (general country engagement, active Mission, active Project) cover the main Operations and Country Engagement use cases. They map onto the existing Contact roles and Mission/Project affiliations without a new taxonomy.
assumptions.rationale: Reusing existing roles and affiliations means no schema change and no new data entry, and it keeps v1 to one view.

assumptions.statement: A rules-based ranking over data the CRM already holds (role, affiliation, Engagement recency, active status) is accurate enough for v1. Coordinators will not designate primaries by hand.
assumptions.rationale: Deterministic rules are simple to build, test, and explain. Because engagement logging already happens, ranking stays current without extra effort from busy Regional Coordinators.

assumptions.statement: The existing Country/Mission access model already controls who may see which contacts and fields, and the new card can inherit it unchanged.
assumptions.rationale: This avoids building or auditing a new permission layer, and the card cannot expose anything the underlying records do not already expose.

assumptions.statement: Contact records already carry, or can derive, an active/inactive or term-end indicator, and Engagement records carry a contact and a date. A single fixed 180-day staleness threshold is a reasonable v1 default.
assumptions.rationale: A fixed constant avoids per-country settings that someone would have to maintain. It can be tuned later from pilot feedback.

assumptions.statement: The users are existing Operations and Country Engagement staff who are already inside the CRM and look up contacts from a Country page. A read-only card in that spot meets the need, with no new navigation or tool.
assumptions.rationale: Placing the feature on a screen people already use means there is no new workflow to adopt and one small UI surface to build.

success_criteria.criterion: For 100% of countries with at least one active contact, the card shows a recommended contact for the general context with zero manual data entry. The number of new required fields for Regional Coordinators is 0.
In a pilot review of 30 countries, spanning regions and with varied engagement history, Regional Coordinators judge the top recommendation correct or acceptable in at least 80% of cases.
In a test dataset, 100% of contacts with no Engagement in 180 days show the 'may be outdated' badge, and 100% of inactive or term-ended contacts are excluded from recommendations.
Permission tests with at least 5 role/country-access combinations show 0 contacts or fields displayed in the card that the user cannot see on the underlying Contact or Country record.
The card renders in under 1 second at p95 for the largest country by contact count, and shows the correct empty-state or fallback label in 100% of test cases with no eligible contact.

challenges.challenge_text: Ranking by most recent Engagement date rewards whoever our staff happened to talk to, not who is authoritative. Example: a Regional Coordinator logs a call with a junior ministry desk officer last week, and that person outranks the Director-level Mission delegate last engaged 100 days ago. The card then tells staff to contact the wrong person on a sensitive mission. Recency is also gameable by incidental logging (mass email, event attendance). Rank role/affiliation match above recency and bound recency as a tiebreaker only, or show why-text that exposes the weak basis.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: Proposer claims 'accurate enough for v1' and relies on a 30-country pilot at 80% acceptance, which means up to 20% wrong recommendations on diplomatically sensitive outreach. No bound on the harm of a wrong top pick is given, and no distinction between a Mission delegate and any other role match.

challenges.challenge_text: Staleness depends on Contact records having a reliable active/term-end flag, which the Proposer only says 'already carry, or can derive'. In practice, when a minister is reshuffled or a ministry contact leaves, nobody updates the Contact record, and the contact stays flagged active. The card then confidently recommends the departed person as the top pick, and the 'may be outdated' badge only appears after 180 days of silence. A contact engaged 20 days ago by email, which bounced or was answered by a successor, shows no warning. 180 days is also wrong for dormant-but-valid relationships (annual-cycle ministries) and too long for fast-turnover posts. Verify the field exists and is populated, and make the 'last verified' or term-end data visible on the card, not only engagement recency.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: A4 is an unverified assumption about the data model, and the fixed 180-day constant is a guess. Engagement date measures our activity, not whether the person still holds the post. No handling exists for a recommended contact whose data is stale but recently engaged.

challenges.challenge_text: Inheriting the existing Country/Mission access model unchanged is not enough because the card aggregates across contexts and ranks. Scenarios: (1) a user with access to Country X but not to Mission M sees a fallback or ranking influenced by Mission-affiliated contacts or engagement history they cannot see, so the 'why' line ('Mission delegate, last engaged 12 days ago') leaks the existence of a restricted mission and the engagement timing of a restricted contact; (2) ranking is computed over all contacts and then filtered, so the absence or position of alternates reveals hidden ones; (3) 'last engaged N days ago' derives from Engagement records that may be more restricted than the Contact record. The 'why' text and the active Mission/Project lists must be computed only over records the viewer is authorized to see, and the success test must cover Engagement and Mission visibility, not just Contact fields.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: The Proposer asserts 'the card cannot expose anything the underlying records do not already expose', but derived data (rank, recency, mission affiliation) is a new disclosure surface. The permission test criterion only checks contacts and fields displayed, not derived values or Mission/Engagement visibility.

challenges.challenge_text: A single authoritative-looking 'recommended contact' on a read-only card invites over-trust and copy-paste outreach, with no signal of confidence. Example: a coordinator new to a country (turnover is high) trusts the card and sends a sensitive message to a ministry contact who is the wrong level or has moved on, with no prompt to verify. Also, the 'may be outdated' badge shown on many contacts in low-engagement countries (most of 100 countries will be quiet most of the time) becomes wallpaper that staff ignore, which is the alert-fatigue case. Define behavior when the top pick is badged or when the top two candidates are close in score, such as showing a 'low confidence, verify before contact' state instead of a confident recommendation.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: A5 presumes users are experienced staff who will sanity-check the card; it ignores new coordinators and the fact that the badge threshold is global. No measure of badge frequency is in the success criteria, so alert fatigue is not tested.

challenges.challenge_text: Three contexts mapped onto existing Contact roles assume the roles are consistently populated and that multiple people can have the same role in a country. Across ~100 countries entered by different coordinators, role values are likely free-text or inconsistent, so 'role match to the context' silently falls through to engagement recency, which compounds C1. Also, falling back from Mission/Project to the general country context may surface a contact who is not cleared for that mission's subject, in effect recommending someone outside the mission's intended circle. Check role data quality before build, and fallback must not suggest contacts not affiliated with the mission without clear labelling and access checks.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: A1 claims no new taxonomy is needed without evidence on role data consistency. The labelled fallback in S5 only covers display, not whether the fallback contact is appropriate for the mission.

challenge_responses.response: Recency was already ranked below role and affiliation, but the scope did not state that it can never outrank them, and the why-text did not show the weak basis. Both fixes are cheap and use existing data. S2 now says recency is a tiebreaker only, the why-text names the deciding rule (e.g. 'No role match; ranked by recent engagement only'), and a test asserts that a role and affiliation match always beats recency. Whether a Director outranks a desk officer within the same role is a seniority or protocol decision. That is a policy question for humans, not product design, and it stays out of scope. If the role data cannot distinguish them, S6 shows 'Verify before contact' rather than a confident pick.

Two cheap fixes. (1) S3 now shows the term-end date and the Contact record's last-updated date on the card where those already exist, so staff see data age as well as engagement recency. No new fields and no verification workflow are added. (2) S6 labels any badged or role-less top pick 'Verify before contact'. Whether the active/term-end field exists and is populated is checked in the pre-build audit; it is a build task, not scope. Not adopted: per-country or per-post thresholds, which are settings someone must maintain, and bounce or successor detection, which needs mail integration. The residual risk is a departed contact with no record update and a recent engagement. It is bounded by the visible record dates and by the fact that recommendations are read-only suggestions. Evidence for revisiting the 180-day constant is the pilot's share of 'Verify' states and coordinator feedback.

The Critic is right that derived values are a disclosure surface. The fix is cheap and adds no permission layer: S4 now applies the existing visibility filter before ranking. Alternates, 'why' text, 'last engaged' dates, Mission/Project lists and fallbacks are computed only over records the viewer can already see, so nothing is ranked and then hidden. A new test covers Mission and Engagement visibility and checks the output equals the card computed over visible records only. If Engagement records are in fact more restricted than Contact records, we inherit that existing rule. Whether any Engagement or Mission data needs a different classification is an institutional data-classification decision for a human, not something this design invents. If no existing Engagement visibility rule can be filtered at read time, that should be escalated.

A single deterministic rule over existing data is cheap and bounds the over-trust risk: S6 replaces 'Recommended' with 'Verify before contact' when the top pick is badged, has no role match, is a fallback, or ties with the second candidate. There is one label per context, not a badge on every row, and there are no scores, settings or queues. For alert fatigue, we measure rather than guess. The pilot reports the share of contexts showing 'Verify', and a share above 50% triggers a rule and threshold review. A dashboard or notifications to chase this are not added.

Two cheap fixes. (1) Role data quality becomes a pre-build read-only audit with a threshold (80% populated and consistent). Below the threshold, role match is dropped for the affected contexts and the card shows 'Verify before contact'. No role-mapping table is built, because that is expensive. Several people with the same role are handled by the tie rule in S6. (2) S5 fallback now states 'not affiliated with this Mission/Project, verify before contact', and the fallback list passes through the same visibility filter as S4. Whether a general-country contact is appropriate for a mission's subject matter is a security-clearance and policy decision. This design does not make that decision, so a human should rule on it. Until then the fallback is only labelled, never presented as a confident recommendation.

Seniority within a role is a protocol decision and the Proposer rightly leaves it out. S6 labels ties 'Verify before contact'. The residual risk is acceptable for an MVP.

final_decision.feature_request: We need a better way to track who is the right person to contact in each country.
final_decision.executive_summary: v1 is a read-only 'Who to contact' card on the Country page. It ranks contacts at read time from existing data (role match, then affiliation, then engagement recency as a tiebreaker only) and applies the existing visibility filter before ranking. The agreed parts of v1 are staleness handling (S3), reuse of the existing access model (S4), and a single 'Verify before contact' confidence label (S6). The main trade-off argued was recency against authority and data quality: the Critic pushed for recency to be a tiebreaker only, for data age to be visible, for visibility filtering before ranking, and for a low-confidence state, and the Proposer adopted cheap rule-based fixes without adding settings, tables, or workflows. The card itself (S1), the ranking (S2), and the empty/fallback states (S5) are pending a human decision on C5, as are the success criteria that measure them. C5 asks whether a general-country contact may be suggested as a fallback for a Mission's subject, and whether role data quality is sufficient.

Automated notifications, reminders, or outreach to confirm contact details, including bounce or successor detection from email
Protocol, seniority, or diplomatic-precedence ranking (a policy decision for humans, not product design)
Availability, time-zone, language, or preferred-channel handling
Escalation chains or formal backup-contact designation
Integrations with external directories or ministry data sources
Custom RBAC or new data-classification labels
success_criteria: In a test dataset, 100% of contacts with no Engagement in 180 days show the 'may be outdated' badge, and 100% of inactive or term-ended contacts are excluded from recommendations. (measures S3)

success_criteria_pending.item: For 100% of countries with at least one active contact, the card shows a recommended contact for the general context with zero manual data entry. The number of new required fields for Regional Coordinators is 0. (measures S1, S2, S5)

In a pilot review of 30 countries, spanning regions and with varied engagement history, Regional Coordinators judge the top recommendation correct or acceptable in at least 80% of cases. (measures S1, S2, S3)

Permission tests with at least 5 role/country-access combinations show 0 contacts or fields displayed in the card that the user cannot see on the underlying Contact or Country record. (measures S4, S1)

The card renders in under 1 second at p95 for the largest country by contact count, and shows the correct empty-state or fallback label in 100% of test cases with no eligible contact. (measures S1, S2, S5)

In a test dataset, a contact with a role match and affiliation outranks any contact without them in 100% of cases regardless of Engagement recency, and 100% of 'why' lines name the deciding rule. (measures S2)

Permission tests with at least 5 access combinations, including a user with Country access but no access to a given Mission and a user with Contact access but no access to its Engagements, show 0 hidden Missions, Engagements, contacts or derived values (rank position, alternates, 'why' text, 'last engaged' date, fallback) in the card, with output identical to the card computed over only the visible records. (measures S4, S1, S2, S5)

In a test dataset, 100% of recommended contacts that are badged, have no role match, are fallbacks, or tie on role and affiliation show 'Verify before contact'. In the 30-country pilot, the share of contexts showing it is reported, and a share above 50% triggers a review of the rule and the 180-day constant. (measures S6, S3, S5)

Before build, a read-only audit of the Contact role field across all ~100 countries reports the share of contacts with a populated, consistent role value. If it is below 80%, role match is dropped from the ranking order for the affected contexts and those contexts show the 'Verify before contact' label. (measures S2, S6)

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: 'Right person' depends on context, and three contexts (general country engagement, active Mission, active Project) cover the main Operations and Country Engagement use cases. They map onto the existing Contact roles and Mission/Project affiliations without a new taxonomy.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: C5 challenged whether existing roles map cleanly onto the three contexts and whether a general-country fallback is appropriate for a Mission. The Proposer added a pre-build role audit and a labelled fallback, and the Critic escalated the clearance/policy part to a human, so C5 ended ESCALATED_TO_HUMAN.

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: A rules-based ranking over data the CRM already holds (role, affiliation, Engagement recency, active status) is accurate enough for v1. Coordinators will not designate primaries by hand.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: C1 challenged ranking by recent engagement. The Proposer revised so recency is a tiebreaker only and the 'why' line names the deciding rule, and the Critic accepted.

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: The existing Country/Mission access model already controls who may see which contacts and fields, and the new card can inherit it unchanged.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: C3 challenged leakage of hidden Mission and Engagement data through derived values. The Proposer revised S4 to filter by visibility before ranking and extended the permission tests, and the Critic accepted.

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: Contact records already carry, or can derive, an active/inactive or term-end indicator, and Engagement records carry a contact and a date. A single fixed 180-day staleness threshold is a reasonable v1 default.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: C2 challenged reliance on an unverified active/term-end field and a fixed 180-day threshold. The Proposer revised S3 to show term-end and last-updated dates and added the 'Verify before contact' label and a pre-build audit, and the Critic accepted with residual risk noted.

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: The users are existing Operations and Country Engagement staff who are already inside the CRM and look up contacts from a Country page. A read-only card in that spot meets the need, with no new navigation or tool.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: C4 challenged over-trust in a single confident recommendation and badge fatigue. The Proposer revised by adding one 'Verify before contact' label per context (S6) and a pilot measure of how often it appears, and the Critic accepted.

open_questions_for_humans.decision_owner: Unassigned: product owner to route (likely Head of Diplomatic Security or Legal for the clearance question)
open_questions_for_humans.question: Is it acceptable for the card to suggest a general-country contact as a labelled fallback ('Fallback: not affiliated with this Mission/Project, verify before contact') for a Mission or Project whose subject that contact may not be cleared for? Engineering cannot make this clearance and policy decision. Until it is made, S1, S2, S5 and their success criteria stay pending. Should the pre-build role-data audit (80% populated and consistent threshold) also proceed on this basis?
